subject: Biology
title: Adrenal Gland Zonation & Stress Physiology
learningObjectives: Identify the 3 histological zones of the Adrenal Cortex: Zona Glomerulosa, Fasciculata, and Reticularis
Describe the physiological actions of Aldosterone and Cortisol (metabolic and immunosuppressive)
Explain the emergency '3F' actions of Adrenal Medulla Catecholamines (Epinephrine 80% and Norepinephrine 20%)
content:
The paired Adrenal Glands (Suprarenal Glands) sit atop each kidney, comprising an outer mesodermal Adrenal Cortex ($80\text{--}90\%$) and an inner ectodermal Adrenal Medulla ($10\text{--}20\%$).

```
                           ADRENAL GLAND ZONATION
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
   ADRENAL CORTEX (Outer Mesodermal)                       ADRENAL MEDULLA (Inner Ectodermal)
   ├── Zona Glomerulosa (Outer) ──► Mineralocorticoids     └── Chromaffin Cells ──► Catecholamines
   ├── Zona Fasciculata (Middle) ──► Glucocorticoids           ├── Epinephrine / Adrenaline (80%)
   └── Zona Reticularis (Inner)  ──► Gonadocorticoids          └── Norepinephrine / Noradrenaline (20%)
```

### 6.1 Cortical Hormones & Functional Profile

1. **Mineralocorticoids (Aldosterone)**: Secreted by Zona Glomerulosa. Acts on kidney DCT and collecting ducts to stimulate $\text{Na}^+$ and water reabsorption and $\text{K}^+/\text{H}^+$ excretion, regulating blood volume and electrolyte balance.
2. **Glucocorticoids (Cortisol)**: Secreted by Zona Fasciculata.
   - **Metabolic Functions**: Stimulates Gluconeogenesis, Lipolysis, and Proteolysis; inhibits cellular glucose uptake (hyperglycemic factor).
   - **Anti-Inflammatory & Immunosuppressive Functions**: Inhibits prostaglandin synthesis, suppresses inflammatory response, reduces histamine release, and depresses antibody production (used clinically to prevent organ transplant rejection).
   - **Stress Adaptation**: Master hormone modulating long-term resistance to physiological stress.
3. **Gonadocorticoids (Adrenal Androgens)**: Secreted by Zona Reticularis. Secretes DHEA and androstenedione, contributing to axillary and pubic hair growth during puberty.

### 6.2 Catecholamines & Emergency Physiology (3F Response)

The Adrenal Medulla functions as a modified post-ganglionic sympathetic ganglion. Its Chromaffin Cells secrete Epinephrine (Adrenaline) and Norepinephrine (Noradrenaline) in response to acute stress ("3F Hormones: Flight, Fight, or Fright").

```
                        CATECHOLAMINE EMERGENCY EFFECTS
                        
   Adrenal Medulla Releases Epinephrine / Norepinephrine
                             │
   ┌─────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┐
   ▼                         ▼                         ▼
   Cardiovascular            Respiratory               Metabolic
   ├── Increases HR & SV     ├── Bronchodilation        ├── Glycogenolysis (Glucose surge)
   ├── Increases Systemic BP └── Increased Ventilation  ├── Lipolysis
   └── Increases Contractility                           └── Piloerection & Pupillary Mydriasis
```

conceptBreakdown.heading: Cushingoid Features from Excess Cortisol
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Hypercortisolemia in Cushing's syndrome induces trunkal adipose redistribution ('Moon Face', 'Buffalo Hump', pendulous abdomen) alongside severe peripheral skeletal muscle wasting due to continuous proteolysis.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Chromaffin Cells as Postganglionic Neurons
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Chromaffin cells of the adrenal medulla are embryologically derived from neural crest ectoderm, receiving direct preganglionic sympathetic cholinergic innervation via the greater splanchnic nerves.
